focus: sk-code-ci contents: which of the seven workflow-authoring rules are machine-enforced today and which are only conventions

graphEvents.label: What workflow-authoring rules does the repo enforce, and where?
Path parity is the only machine-enforced workflow rule

label: Exactly one workflow-authoring rule is machine-enforced: check-gate-inputs.sh owns filter-twins (path parity), workflow-inputs (run inputs resolve), parser-miss (unparseable shapes fail closed) and gate-files, and it enumerates workflows by glob so a new file is covered with no registry to update. sk-code-ci must cite this checker rather than restate the twin rule.

The README row rule is 100% satisfied and 0% enforced: the coverage table names 33 workflows and disk holds 33, with no missing row and no dangling row, but no script reads workflows/README (rg -l returns only specs/ artifacts). A new workflow with no row passes every gate, which makes a table-vs-disk diff the cheapest useful check /doctor:ci can add.

SHA pinning is 100% satisfied and unenforced: every uses: in .github/workflows and .github/actions is a full commit SHA with a trailing version comment (zero @vN/@main hits), the policy is stated only as a YAML comment in dependabot.yml, and the github-actions dependabot group is what keeps the pins current. A 40-hex check on the uses: value would make the invariant survive a pasted @v4.

set -euo pipefail is already owned doctrine, not a workflow rule: it lives at shell-checklist.md:63 under sk-code-skilled, 29 of 33 workflows carry it, and the four that do not are advisory-checks, dependabot-auto-merge, sk-code-script-tests and sk-git-script-tests. sk-code-ci should carry one routing sentence ('a run: block is shell, see shell-checklist') rather than a second copy of the rule, which is the drift class check-rule-copies.test.sh exists to catch.

Three rules are largely not followed and none is enforced: timeout-minutes in 6 of 33 workflows, a top-level permissions: block in 21 of 33 (the other 12 have none at job level either and inherit the default token scope, wider than the contents: read the compliant workflows set), and concurrency in 1 of 33 (trigger-index-rebuild, deliberately cancel-in-progress: false because it commits). Retrofitting all three is 71 edits across 33 files.

The fork and secret surface is small and clean: pull_request_target appears zero times in .github/workflows, and secrets. appears three times in two files (dependabot-auto-merge's GITHUB_TOKEN twice, trigger-index-rebuild's TRIGGER_INDEX_PUSH_TOKEN with a github.token fallback). The rule is therefore a two-name allowlist plus a pull_request_target prohibition, checkable by rg.

The enforcement map that references/workflow-yaml-standards.md must carry: path parity, run-input resolution and parser-miss are ENFORCED by check-gate-inputs.sh and cited not restated; set -euo pipefail is DOCTRINE owned by shell-checklist.md and routed; README row, SHA pinning, timeouts, permissions, concurrency and fork/secret safety are CONVENTIONS with no enforcer. An entry that neither cites an enforcer nor admits the absence reads like a gate and behaves like a suggestion.
A standards entry states its rule and then either names the script that enforces it or says nothing does; it never restates a rule a checker already owns.

direction: Have sk-code-ci restate the path-parity twin rule in prose so reviewers do not need to open check-gate-inputs.sh
reason: The checker is fail-closed, fixture-tested and glob-enumerated, so a prose copy can only drift from it; sk-code-review already has check-rule-copies.test.sh to catch exactly that duplication.

direction: Treat the 12 workflows without a permissions: block as a scaffold-template defect to be fixed by /doctor:ci scaffold
reason: Scaffold only affects workflows written after the template lands; the 12 existing files need a customize sweep, so the two are separate work items with separate risk.
